title: Come and See the Works of God
superscription: For the choirmaster. A song. A Psalm.

verses.text: Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth!
Sing the glory of His name; make His praise glorious.
Say to God, "How awesome are Your deeds! So great is Your power that Your enemies cower before You.
All the earth bows down to You; they sing praise to You; they sing praise to Your name." Selah
Come and see the works of God; how awesome are His deeds toward mankind.
He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot; there we rejoiced in Him.
He rules forever by His power; His eyes watch the nations. Do not let the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah
Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of His praise be heard.
He preserves our lives and keeps our feet from slipping.
For You, O God, have tested us; You have refined us like silver.
You led us into the net; You laid burdens on our backs.
You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but You brought us into abundance.
I will enter Your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to You—
the vows that my lips promised and my mouth spoke in my distress.
I will offer You fatlings as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams; I will offer bulls and goats. Selah
Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will declare what He has done for me.
I cried out to Him with my mouth and praised Him with my tongue.
If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
But God has surely heard; He has attended to the sound of my prayer.
Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer or withheld from me His loving devotion!

context.author: Not named; the title says only “a song, a Psalm.”
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: “Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth!” (v.1). “Come and see the works of God; how awesome are His deeds toward mankind. He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot” (vv.5-6). The people remember hard times as God’s refining: “For You, O God, have tested us; You have refined us like silver… we went through fire and water, but You brought us into abundance” (vv.10-12). Then one voice speaks: “I will enter Your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to You” (v.13). “Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will declare what He has done for me” (v.16). “If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened. But God has surely heard” (vv.18-19).
context.custom: A person rescued from trouble came to the Temple to pay the vow he had made, with sacrifices and a public testimony to the gathered worshipers (vv.13-16). Silver was refined in fire to remove dross (v.10). “Fire and water” was a proverbial phrase for every kind of danger (Isaiah 43:2).
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 67 prays that God’s face would shine so that all nations would know Him.
context.timelineBible: “They passed through the waters on foot” recalls both the Red Sea (Exodus 14:21-22) and the Jordan (Joshua 3:14-17). Peter says trials refine faith like gold (1 Peter 1:6-7). The healed blind man said, “God does not listen to sinners” (John 9:31), a thought like v.18.

translation.meaning: To shout, raise a shout of joy or battle.
Burnt offering, wholly burned on the altar.

overview.summary: All the earth is called to praise God who brought Israel through sea and fire; then one worshiper pays his vows and tells what God has done for him.
overview.settingLine: A worshiper paying vows before the crowd.

archaeology.t: Large altars for burnt offerings, as at Beersheba.
Hoards of cut silver show how silver was weighed and refined.

overview.discussion: “Come and listen… I will declare what He has done for me” (v.16). What has God done for me that someone else needs to hear?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: Not named
overview.genre: Thanksgiving of the nation and of one worshiper
